_about: Subjective view per upcoming match, keyed by ESPN match id, written by a scheduled task from recent news. Shown in each stat's 'Why' box and next to 'Our call'; never mixed into the numbers. Per stat (goals, corners, cards, shots, shots_on_target): {lean: higher|lower|same, call: short judgement call, text: reasoning}. Also: overall, sources (URLs), written_at (ISO). Never use 'lock', 'sure thing' or 'guaranteed'.

401884736.overall: Bayern are top with 21 points from nine games and host 15th-placed Cologne, who have not won in four league games and scored only two goals in that run. Vincent Kompany returns to the touchline for the first time since collapsing on 23 October; at Thursday's press conference he said Musiala is available and will probably be involved, while Luis Díaz is not ready yet (he hopes within seven days) and Davies, Neuer, Gnabry and Saibari stay out, all already counted by the numbers. Cologne's René Wagner is without Dallinga, Hübers, Skhiri, van den Berg and Rondic (all counted) and is expected to set up with a back five, with Ache fit but likely on the bench. Robin Braun referees, and his above-average card record is already in the numbers. Match-day check: no new injuries or surprises, so the view is unchanged.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.7 goals and already take about 12% off Bayern's attack for Díaz and Musiala as if both are fully out. Kompany confirmed on Thursday that Díaz is still a week away but Musiala is available and will probably play some part, which the numbers don't see, so I nudge up just 1%, to about 3.74. Cologne without Dallinga and Skhiri is already counted.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.9 corners, with Bayern's recent run of corners (37 in six) already added. Cologne are expected to line up with a back five and defend deep, then break quickly, which is the one-sided pattern the numbers already expect, so I stay at 10.9.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.1 cards and already add about 9% for referee Robin Braun (4.4 cards a game against a 3.9 average) plus Cologne's high recent card count (17 in six). Wagner wants his players to 'go where it hurts', but that fits the same pattern the numbers count, so I stay at 4.1.

shots.text: The numbers say 32.0 shots and already add 7.5% for Bayern's hot shooting run (127 shots in six). Bayern's attack around Kane, Olise, Karl and Brown is near full strength apart from Díaz, who is counted, so I stay at 32.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 12.4 shots on target, already lifted 11% for Bayern's recent accuracy. Musiala off the bench adds a little, but that is in the small goals nudge, and Cologne's weak attack without Dallinga is counted, so I stay at 12.4.

401884732.overall: Union are 16th with 7 points and only 48 shots in their last six, and Mauro Lustrinelli's side host Leipzig, 4th with four wins in five after a 5-2 win over Augsburg. Union's injury news got worse overnight: the Berliner Zeitung (19 Nov) reports Juranovic ill, so the numbers are right to count him out (about -8% on Union's goals), while Ligainsider reports Janik Haberer, Union's top scorer this season per Sports Mole, out with an illness and Burcu missing training; Uduokhai, Nsoki and Skov are out, and captain Trimmel is back. The numbers count Juranovic, Skov and Nsoki but not Haberer or Uduokhai. Leipzig miss Guiu and Ouedraogo (counted), with the Bundesliga's predicted XI built around Nusa, Nkunku, Gruda and Romulo. Christian Dingert referees; his near-average record (3.8 a game) is already in the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.9 goals and already take about 8% off Union for Juranovic, who the Berliner Zeitung now reports ill, so that cut holds. What they don't see is Haberer, Union's top scorer, out ill and Burcu doubtful, for a side that has scored little lately, so I go 5% lower, to about 2.8 (was -3, when Juranovic looked set to return).

corners.text: The numbers say 9.2 corners, already cut for both sides' low recent corner counts (Union 18, Leipzig 22 in six). Leipzig win their corners down the flanks through Nusa and Raum and Union rely on long balls and set pieces whoever plays, which the numbers already see, so I stay at 9.2.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.8 cards and already add Union's rough recent run (18 cards in six) while trimming a little for referee Dingert, who shows about 3.8 a game. Lustrinelli wants an intense, brave Union, and Trimmel's return adds an experienced defender, but that is the same pattern the numbers already add for, so I stay at 3.8.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.1 shots and already cut Union's shots 13% for their recent drought. Haberer, their top scorer, is out ill and Burcu is doubtful, and Juranovic's crosses from the left are also missing, so Union's attack is thinner than the numbers assume; I go 4% lower, to about 24.1 (was -3).

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.3 shots on target, with Leipzig's recent accuracy (+8%) and Union's poor one (11 on target in six) already counted. Losing Haberer, Union's most reliable finisher, takes away some of their few good chances, so I go 4% lower, to about 8.9 (was -3).

401884735.overall: Leverkusen are 5th with 16 points and host Paderborn, 13th but unbeaten in four with the league's best defensive start in their history (11 conceded). Carles Martinez has most of his attack back: Sports Mole's preview and the Bundesliga's predicted XI both have Diaby and Maza starting behind Schick (eight goals), while Bulinews expects Kofane and Tella back too and Sports Mole still lists Tella, Terrier and Kofane out. The numbers count Diaby, Tella, Doue, Terrier and Eichhorn as missing, so Diaby's return is the clear thing they miss. Paderborn's coach Ralf Kettemann expects a game 'focused on defending our own goal'; they miss Gayret, with Hoffmeier, Klaas and others counted. Tobias Reichel referees and his near-average record (4.0 a game) is already in the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals and take about 3% off Leverkusen for Diaby, who two predicted lineups now have starting, with Maza cleared after his Algeria knock. Paderborn plan to defend deep and have conceded only 11 in nine, and reports differ on Kofane and Tella, so I go only 3% higher, to about 2.7 (was +4).

corners.text: The numbers say 11.4 corners, with Leverkusen expected to win about 8 against a Paderborn back three that will sit deep. Diaby and Maza returning changes who finishes moves more than how often Leverkusen reach the byline, so I stay at 11.4.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.6 cards, with referee Reichel (4.0 a game) adding about 3%. Paderborn's low recent card count is already in the numbers, and a deep block facing lots of possession usually means fouls when chasing, which their record also shows, so I stay at 3.6.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.9 shots, already lifted slightly for both sides' recent volume. Leverkusen kept shooting a lot (102 in six) even with forwards missing, so Diaby's and Maza's returns mostly help quality, not volume, and I stay at 31.9.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.3 shots on target. With Diaby back on the right and Maza at number 10 behind Schick, Leverkusen's finishing options are better than the numbers assume, though Paderborn's tight defence limits clear looks, so I go 2% higher, to about 10.5 (was +3).

401884731.overall: Bottom side Gladbach (4 points, the league's worst defence with 25 conceded) host Dortmund, 2nd, unbeaten, level with Bayern and with the league's best defence (7 conceded). Gladbach are without the banned Itakura and the injured Kleindienst, Leopold, Leszczynski and Ullrich; the numbers count Bolin and Ullrich for goals, though Sports Mole's predicted XI has Bolin starting while the Bundesliga's does not. For Dortmund, Can, Konstantelias and Lerma are out, and Guirassy, Anton and Chukwuemeka were late fitness calls (BVB site, Bulinews); Sports Mole now expects Guirassy on the bench with Fabio Silva leading the line, while Anton is in both predicted XIs. Alexander Blessin expects a fight and Niko Kovac warned against underestimating Gladbach. Robert Hartmann referees and his record (4.0 a game) is close to average.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals, already taking Bolin and Ullrich off Gladbach. What they can't see is Guirassy, Dortmund's main striker, likely starting on the bench after his muscle problem, with Fabio Silva expected to lead the line, and Gladbach still without captain Kleindienst; I go 3% lower, to about 2.7 (was -2).

corners.text: The numbers say 9.2 corners, already nudged up for Dortmund's recent count (37 in six). Gladbach play a back three and look to break, and Dortmund build through their wing-backs, both of which the numbers already expect, so I stay at 9.2.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.6 cards and already add a big 22% for Gladbach's recent card spike (21 in six), including Itakura's sending-off that bans him here. Blessin wants a fight in a full stadium, but that is the same pattern the numbers already add for, and referee Hartmann is close to average, so I stay at 4.6.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.2 shots, already lifted for both sides' recent shooting (Gladbach 93, Dortmund 96 in six). Kovac plans to play his fit first-choice players, so a Guirassy-less attack changes who shoots more than how often, and I stay at 28.2.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.7 shots on target. Guirassy, Dortmund's most accurate finisher, is likely only a bench option and Gladbach miss Kleindienst, so both sides' best shooters are short of a start, and I go 3% lower, to about 9.4 (was -2).

401884734.overall: Frankfurt (10th) and Hoffenheim (9th) are level on 12 points in a mid-table game with little extra at stake; the last 11 meetings all had at least four goals and both teams scored in the last 13 (Bundesliga.com). Adi Huetter is without the banned Elias Baum (counted), Koch is fit again, but Can Uzun came back from international duty with a cold and hessenschau (19 Nov) expects him to miss out, which the numbers don't know. Hoffenheim's defence is thin, with Hajdari, Hranac, Gendrey and De Cat out, and the numbers only count these for Frankfurt's goals through Conte's line, not the defenders; one hessenschau headline (20 Nov) says Hoffenheim have Bambase Conte back, though the numbers take about 11% off their goals for him. Max Burda referees; his short record is just below average and already counted.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.6 goals and take about 11% off Hoffenheim for Conte, whom one hessenschau report says is back, while they give Frankfurt nothing for Hoffenheim's four missing defenders. Uzun's likely absence costs Frankfurt some creativity, and Conte's return rests on one source, so I go 4% higher, to about 3.7 (was +2).

corners.text: The numbers say 10.2 corners, already nudged up for Hoffenheim's recent count (37 in six). A reshuffled Hoffenheim back line may concede more chances but not clearly more corners, and both sides press high rather than camp on the flanks, so I stay at 10.2.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.8 cards, with recent counts, head-to-head and referee Burda's slightly low record already in them. Huetter and Ilzer both expect a high-intensity, aggressive game (Koch calls intensity the key factor), but both teams always play that way and it is in their records, so I stay at 3.8.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.3 shots and already add Hoffenheim's recent volume (101 in six, +12%). Their gaps at the back affect chance quality more than the total, and Uzun's absence trims Frankfurt's long-range shooting, so the two roughly cancel and I stay at 28.3.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.1 shots on target. Hoffenheim's makeshift defence should give Frankfurt's strikers Ebnoutalib and Burkardt cleaner looks, and Conte may be back up front, partly offset by losing Uzun, so I go 2% higher, to about 10.3 (was 0).

401884728.overall: Promoted Elversberg (7th, 13 points, unbeaten at home except against Bayern per Julian Schuster) host Freiburg (3rd, 19 points, three wins in their last four including 2-0 over Union) in the clubs' first league meeting. Elversberg have conceded 18 goals in nine and their first-choice centre-backs are in doubt: the Bundesliga's predicted XI pairs Rohr and Le Joncour, without Seifert and captain Pinckert. Right-back Gyamerah, whom the numbers count as out (adding about 6% to Freiburg's goals), is in that predicted XI. Freiburg miss Muslija (counted) and the banned Berkay Yilmaz, not a regular, and are expected with Beste, Suzuki and Matanovic. Richard Hempel referees with only two games on record, which the numbers blend towards the average.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.2 goals and add about 6% to Freiburg's goals for Gyamerah being out, but he is in the predicted XI, so that boost is too big. Elversberg are also likely without both first-choice centre-backs, Seifert and Pinckert, which the numbers don't see, so the two roughly cancel and I stay at 3.2.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.9 corners, with Freiburg's recent run of corners (30 in six) already added. Freiburg's wide play through Beste and Treu wins most of their corners and Elversberg concede plenty (44 in six), both in the numbers, so I stay at 9.9.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.2 cards. Referee Hempel has only two games on record, which the numbers already blend towards the average, and neither side's recent card counts stand out; a stand-in centre-back pairing for Elversberg is only a small hunch for more fouls, so I stay at 3.2.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.1 shots, with Freiburg expected to shoot more. Elversberg have allowed 103 shots in their last six and Freiburg have been shooting above their usual level; both are already counted, so I keep 28.1.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.4 shots on target. Freiburg's accuracy has dipped lately (already counted), and the centre-back doubts at Elversberg and Gyamerah's return pull in opposite directions, so I stay at 8.4.

401884729.overall: Schalke (17th, 6 points, seven games without a win in all competitions) host Stuttgart (8th, 12 points, two league wins in a row) at 18:30 in front of about 60,000; Schalke have still not scored a home goal this season, though they have conceded just 11. Moussa Sylla is back in the squad for the first time since matchday 5 and may start, with Gantenbein and Bachmann also available (90min, Sky, Flashscore), while top scorer Robin Gosens, back in partial training after his knee knock, is at best a bench option; Becker and Woeber are out and already counted. Stuttgart are still without Angelo Stiller (adductor) and Luca Jaquez (rib), both on the numbers' list, while Josha Vagnoman is back in team training and Leo Sauer trained fully on Thursday; Stuttgart play at Inter in the Champions League on Wednesday. Sebastian Hoeness expects a passionate Schalke and wants high intensity and runs in behind; Daniel Siebert referees, and his slightly higher card record is already added.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.1 goals and already take off for Woeber at Schalke and for Stiller and Vagnoman at Stuttgart. Gosens, Schalke's top scorer, is not expected to start, which the numbers can't see, but Sylla's return up front and Vagnoman being back in training soften that, so I trim only 2%, to about 2.06.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.5 corners, with Stuttgart expected to win about 6 of them. Schalke defend deep and look to counter, which hands visitors corners, and Hoeness wants his side to run in behind and down the wings, but both habits are already in the teams' records, so I stay at 10.5.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.6 cards and already add about 8% for referee Daniel Siebert (4.1 a game) plus a little for Schalke's recent games. Hoeness expects a physical, passionate home side in front of 60,000, but that is how Schalke play every home game and it is in their record, so I stay at 3.6.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.9 shots. Schalke's attack produces few shots and will likely start without Gosens, and Stuttgart still miss their main midfield passer Stiller, whom the numbers count only for goals, not shot volume; Sylla's return gives Schalke a target up front, so the trim stays small, 2%, to about 27.3.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.6 shots on target and already cut Schalke's for their poor recent accuracy (13 on target in six). Gosens unlikely to start and Stiller out make both build-ups a bit poorer, while Sylla's comeback gives Schalke a finisher back, so I trim 2%, to about 9.4.

401884733.overall: Two struggling sides meet at the WWK Arena: Augsburg (near the bottom with 9 points) are seven league games without a win under Manuel Baum, conceding at least twice in six of them and losing 5-2 at Leipzig last time, while Mainz (12th, 10 points) have lost four competitive games in a row, though they won their first three league away games and are unbeaten in five meetings with Augsburg. Augsburg miss Banks (ligament), Matsima (muscle tear), Massengo (muscle), Brackelmann (illness) and Mounie (knee), so their back three is patched up with Gouweleeuw, Keitel and Bah expected; the numbers count these absences, including about +6% on Mainz's goals for each missing regular defender. Gregoritsch, Augsburg's top scorer, is expected back in the starting side after being benched at Leipzig (Augsburg took one point from the three games he did not start), and Mainz miss Kohr until January with Silas not ready, both counted. Referee Martin Petersen's high card record (4.5 a game, +14%) is in the numbers, as is both sides' leaky recent form; with no new absences since yesterday, I keep the numbers on every stat.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.3 goals, already lifted by both leaky defences' recent form and counting Brackelmann, Massengo and Matsima out (Augsburg lose some goals, Mainz gain about 6% per missing defender). Gregoritsch starting again is his normal role rather than a change, and Mainz's Tietz and Becker pairing is unchanged, so I stay at 3.3.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.8 corners, with Augsburg winning slightly more at home. Both teams are expected in a back three with wing-backs (Wolf and Behrens for Augsburg, Caci and Mwene for Mainz), which matches how they have played all season, so I stay at 9.8.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.3 cards, already including about 14% for referee Petersen and Mainz's high recent count. Mainz's combative Kohr and Augsburg's Massengo are out, but both are on the missing list the numbers already know, so I drop yesterday's small trim; both coaches expect a game of duels between two sides under pressure, which fits the numbers, so I stay at 5.3.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.8 shots, already lifted by Augsburg's big recent volume (+20%) and Mainz's (+8%). Augsburg are expected to play on the break with Gregoritsch as the target man, and Mainz have scored only four in their four defeats, which fits their records, so I stay at 31.8.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.8 shots on target, with momentum adding for both (+14% Augsburg, +6% Mainz). Augsburg's reshuffled back line is already in the numbers through the missing defenders, and no new absence has been reported since yesterday, so I stay at 10.8.

401884730.overall: The 111th Nordderby: Daniel Thioune's Werder (6th, 15 points, unbeaten at home, and Thioune has just signed a contract extension) host Merlin Polzin's Hamburg (11th, 12 points, three league wins in a row, the last 3-1 against Gladbach, but weak away), and Werder have won eight of their last nine top-flight home games against Hamburg. Werder are without top creator Marco Gruell (calf; 90min reported earlier in the week that his derby place was open, and the Bundesliga's match-day predicted side still leaves him out) and Mitchell Weiser; the numbers count Weiser but not Gruell, and the predicted attack is Njinmah, Chuki and Dinkci behind Fuellkrug, the league's top scorer with nine goals, six from set pieces. Hamburg miss Remberg, Nadir, Torunarigha, Sambi Lokonga and Poulsen (Poulsen and Sambi Lokonga counted for goals), with Daka up front and Muheim, who has scored three times from distance, in midfield. Referee Florian Badstuebner's low card record (-23%) and the derby boost (+39%) are both in the numbers; confirmed XIs were not out when I wrote this, so the view keeps the morning sizes.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals, already taking about 12% off Hamburg for Poulsen and 3% for Sambi Lokonga, and 4% off Werder for Weiser. Gruell, Werder's main creator (two goals, six assists), is not on the numbers' list and the Bundesliga's match-day predicted side again has Njinmah and Chuki instead, so I keep -6, about 2.5 goals; Fuellkrug's set pieces keep Werder dangerous even without him.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners, most of them for Werder at home against Hamburg's back three with wing-backs. Losing Gruell and Weiser costs Werder some wide play, but Njinmah's pace and Dinkci on the flanks plus Werder's set-piece focus around Fuellkrug should still win corners, so nothing points clearly either way and I stay at 9.4.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.3 cards: they add 39% for the derby but take 23% off for referee Badstuebner, who shows only 3.1 cards a game, and both sides have been booked less than usual lately (all counted). The build-up is heated, with ex-Hamburg players facing whistles, but that is the normal derby feel the numbers already add, so I stay at 4.3.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.1 shots, lifted by Werder's strong recent volume (+20%), including 21 shots at Stuttgart, much of it built through Gruell. With Gruell out and Weiser (counted for goals only) missing on the right, Werder lose two of their main suppliers, so I keep -4, about 29.9 shots.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.8 shots on target, with Werder's 43 on target in six games already added (+15%). Without Gruell, who set up many of those chances, Werder's openings should be fewer and less clean, while Hamburg get Daka and Muheim's long-range shooting back, which the numbers already expect, so I keep -5, about 10.3 shots on target.

401883112.overall: A relegation fight in Encamp on Friday night: FC Andorra are 21st with 11 points and no win in four, Leganés 16th with 15 after beating Burgos 3-1, Luis Carrión's first league win in charge. Andorra are without goalkeeper Jesús Owono (12-match ban) and centre-back Diego Alende (red card), both already in the numbers, plus midfielder Théo Le Normand; reports differ on Gael Alonso (back per Thursday's previews, still a doubt per El Gol Digital). Leganés get Javi Montero back from a ban and Gharbi is an option to start, while one report says Rubén Peña and Pulido have knocks and Carrión called a few players 'a bit iffy'. Carrión wants a high press and useful possession, which could cut into the long spells of Andorra pressure the numbers expect. José Luis Guzmán Mansilla referees, and his low card record is already in the numbers; match-day news changed nothing in the view.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals and already add about 6% to Leganés' goals for Alende's ban. Andorra have conceded 24 in 13 and keep giving away early goals, while Leganés have Millán in form and Montero back; but with Gael Alonso back and Bomba expected to start, Andorra's back line is not as patched-up as feared, so I stay at 2.8.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners, 5.8 of them Andorra's, as a home side that usually has the ball and pushes up. Carrión wants Leganés to keep the ball and press high, which could trim Andorra's share a little, but Leganés' recent habit of conceding corners is already in momentum (+3.9%), so I stay at 9.4.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.2 cards: both sides have been booked a lot lately (+11% and +6.6% momentum) and the referee, José Luis Guzmán Mansilla, averages 4.7 cards a game, which already takes about 13% off. It is a tense game between two bottom-five sides, but the previews point to no extra needle beyond that, so I stay at 5.2.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.2 shots, about 18 of them Andorra's, which assumes Leganés sit deep. Carrión said on Thursday he wants a high press and more action in the opponent's half, and Manso also noted Leganés now keep more of the ball, so Andorra may get fewer long spells of pressure; I trim a little, to about 26.4. Leganés' high shots conceded lately are already in momentum (+7%).

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.6 shots on target, with Andorra's recent accuracy already in momentum (+7.4%). With Bomba and Gael Alonso available, Andorra's defence should be close to its usual shape apart from Alende, who is already counted, and the small trim to shots is too little to move this, so I stay at 9.6.

401882299.overall: Sabadell (14th, five league games without a win, only 12 goals in 14 games) host Granada (3rd, six straight league wins, one goal conceded in their last five). Sabadell are unbeaten at home (three wins, three draws), but Ferran Costa has about a third of the squad out: besides Gioacchini (out for the season) and the suspended Català, which the numbers count, Urri, Quadri Liameed, Eneko Aguilar, Codina, Pipa, Xavi Moreno and Nuamah are unavailable, and Costa said the team could barely train this week. Granada have almost everyone: only Casadesús is injured and Owen Emeka is with Spain at the Under-17 World Cup, while Diallo and Arnaiz are back on the bench; Pacheta is expected to repeat the XI that beat Las Palmas and has talked about using three strikers. Referee Rafael Sánchez López shows fewer cards than average and the numbers already take that off.

goals.text: The numbers say 1.9 goals and already take off Gioacchini, Sabadell's top scorer with 3 goals, plus their poor recent scoring. I lean slightly lower to about 1.8: Sabadell are also without Urri, Liameed and several other squad players the numbers don't see and barely trained this week, while Granada's back line (Juanjo Flores, Lama, Alberto Flores in goal) has conceded once in five games.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.4 corners, and they already count both sides' slightly low corner counts lately. Sabadell are direct and strong at set pieces and Granada may push more men forward if Pacheta goes with three strikers, but neither clearly changes the corner count, so I stay at 8.4.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.4 cards: they add a little for Sabadell's high card count (41 yellows and 2 reds this season, Català banned after a red) and take a lot off for referee Rafael Sánchez López, who averages 4.5 cards a game against a league 5.3. Granada are a clean side (25 yellows, no reds); Pacheta calls Sabadell the team that runs the most, which can mean fouls, but nothing here is new to the numbers, so I stay at 4.4.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.1 shots, with 17.1 for Sabadell after a boost for recent form against Granada. I lean lower to about 25.7: Sabadell's attack is thin with Gioacchini, Urri, Liameed and others out and a disrupted week of training, and Granada have been very hard to create against lately.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 7.8 shots on target. Sabadell have put only 17 on target in their last six and now lose more attacking players the numbers don't know about, while Granada have conceded once in five games, so I trim it to about 7.5.

401883108.overall: A relegation six-pointer: Real Sociedad II (18th, 13 points, three unbeaten after six straight defeats) host Cádiz (20th, 11 points), who have not won away in 12 league games. Jon Ansotegi's side lists Ander Barrenetxea as injured and Mamadou Sarr, Beitia, Marchal and Dani Díaz as doubts; the numbers count only Jon Balda's ban (one preview still names Balda in the XI, so treat that as unclear). Cádiz lose Sergio Arribas to a fifth yellow card, reported by two outlets and not in the numbers, but get Jandro Orellana, Bojan Kovacevic and Álvaro García Pascual back; Borja Jiménez says his side lacks accuracy in transitions. Referee Saúl Ais Reig is close to the league average on cards and the numbers add a little for him.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals, already adjusting for Balda's ban on both sides and two past meetings. I lean slightly lower to about 2.6: Cádiz have scored little away and now lose Sergio Arribas to suspension, Real Sociedad II have several attackers doubtful, and a relegation clash between two nervous sides tends to be tight; Orellana's return to Cádiz's midfield partly offsets it.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners and already add for Real Sociedad II's high corner count in their last six (38). I found nothing that changes how either side wins corners, so I stay at 9.4.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.4 cards and already add a bit for referee Saúl Ais Reig (5.5 a game) and recent form. I lean slightly higher to about 5.6 because this is a bottom-of-the-table six-pointer the numbers carry no stakes adjustment for, and Cádiz have players near bans (Borja Vázquez is one yellow from a suspension).

shots.text: The numbers say 27.3 shots, already boosting Real Sociedad II strongly for 98 shots in their last six and trimming Cádiz for their weak attacking form. Arribas's absence and the young hosts' doubts point slightly down but the momentum figures already reflect much of this, so I stay at 27.3.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.3 shots on target, with Cádiz trimmed for 19 on target in their last six. Without Arribas Cádiz lose some creativity, but García Pascual is back up front, so nothing points clearly either way and I stay at 8.3.

401882301.overall: Castellón (2nd, 30 points, unbeaten at home, only 5 goals conceded in 13 games) can go top with a win over Eldense (16th), who ended a three-game losing run by beating Sabadell. Castellón's top scorer Israel Suero (6 of their 24 goals) is out with a physical problem, confirmed by Pablo Hernández on Friday and not counted by the numbers; Fran Castillo and Rodrigo Rêgo are also out besides Brignani, and today's Castellón Plaza preview says a virus has hit several players, with the coach deciding on them at the last minute, while Matías Orozco is back from Colombia duty. Eldense lose captain Jesús Clemente (dislocated shoulder) and Fidel Chaves (muscle problem), neither counted by the numbers, while Guirao is fit again; Javi Calleja plans to press man-to-man, contest possession and take risks. It is a regional match with a tribute to Jesús de Miguel, and referee Pablo Morales Moreno is slightly below average on cards.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals, 2.0 of them for Castellón. I lean lower because Israel Suero, scorer of a quarter of Castellón's league goals, is out and the numbers don't know it, and today's preview adds a virus in the Castellón squad; Eldense are also without Fidel Chaves and Castellón's defence has conceded only 5 in 13, so I go 8% lower, to about 2.6 (a point more than before because of the virus).

corners.text: The numbers say 9.5 corners and already trim Eldense for 19 corners in their last six. Castellón are one of the sides that keep the ball most and should still pin Eldense back even without Suero, while Eldense's plan to contest possession cuts the other way, so I stay at 9.5.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.3 cards: they add a lot for Eldense's recent cards (20 in six) and take a little off for referee Pablo Morales Moreno (4.6 a game in 7 games). I lean slightly higher to about 5.5 because it is a regional match the numbers do not flag as a derby and Calleja wants aggressive man-to-man pressing all over the pitch, which tends to bring fouls.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.6 shots and already trim Castellón for a quieter recent spell. Without Suero, and with a virus going through the squad, Castellón lose some of their attacking edge, and Eldense will try to slow the game by contesting the ball, so I trim 4%, to about 23.6.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.7 shots on target. Suero's absence matters most here, since he is the player who turns Castellón's possession into efforts on goal, and the reported virus may weaken their attack further, so I lower it 6%, to about 8.2.

401883107.overall: Tenerife (13th, 18 points, a game in hand) host Mallorca (7th, one point off the play-offs) in the second home game since the death of former player Jesús de Miguel, whom Mallorca honoured at the stadium on Friday. Both sides are tired: Tenerife play their third game in six days after beating Ceuta and winning 2-5 at Badajoz in the cup, and Álvaro Cervera has said his side's physical numbers are not good right now; Mallorca needed extra time to beat Alcoyano in the cup and had two days to recover. Mallorca are without Morlanes, David López, Antonio Sánchez, John Donald and others (the listed ones are in the numbers), with Alberto Moreno and Puigmal doubts, while Raíllo, Valjent, Cerdà and Dani Luna are available; Mallorca have gone five games without a clean sheet and their sporting director was dismissed this week. LaLiga's match page lists Juan Gordillo Escamilla first among the officials, matching the referee the numbers already add for (7.8 cards a game); a match-day check found no new injuries or lineup news, so the view from this morning stands.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.1 goals. Two points pull in opposite directions: Cervera's Tenerife defend deep and concede little and both teams are tired, but Mallorca have gone five games without a clean sheet and Enric Gallego is a constant threat. The numbers already count both sides' recent scoring, so I stay at 2.1.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.0 corners and already add for Mallorca's 43 corners in their last six. Tenerife sitting deep and breaking could feed Mallorca corners, but that is the pattern the numbers already see and no lineup news changes it, so I stay at 9.0.

cards.text: The numbers say 6.6 cards, already raised a lot for referee Juan Gordillo Escamilla (7.8 a game in 6 games, LaLiga's page still lists him) and for both sides' recent cards. Tired legs late in the game can bring fouls, but the atmosphere around the De Miguel tribute has been one of respect between the clubs, so I add nothing and stay at 6.6.

shots.text: The numbers say 22.4 shots. I lean slightly lower to about 21.5 because Tenerife play their third game in six days (Cervera says their physical numbers are not good) and Mallorca had only two days after an extra-time cup tie, which the numbers can't see, and Cervera's side limits chances at home.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 6.7 shots on target. For the same fatigue reasons and Tenerife's tight defending, I trim it a little to about 6.5.

401882300.overall: Córdoba (10th, 20 points, five games unbeaten and three straight home wins) host Real Oviedo (9th, 21 points), with both a step from the play-off places. Córdoba drew 3-3 at Mallorca; Diarra joins the long-term absentees, while Kevin Medina and Cristian Carracedo are back in the squad. Oviedo lost 1-2 to Girona in Raúl González's first game after Julián Calero was sacked; they are poor at home but fourth-best away. EFE now confirms Alberto Reina and Pablo Sáenz are left out along with the long-term injured Dani Calvo and Chris Ramos, all of which the numbers already take off, and Enzo Pérez returns to replace Reina. Daniel Palencia of the Basque committee referees; his slightly above-average card record is already in the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.9 goals and already take off Oviedo's missing Reina, Sáenz, Calvo and Chris Ramos while adding for both sides' strong recent scoring (Córdoba have scored in nine straight league games, Oviedo in ten). Reina is now confirmed out rather than doubtful, but the numbers already assumed that, and Córdoba's open style keeps the total high, so I stay at 2.9.

corners.text: The numbers say 11.5 corners and already add a lot for Córdoba's 48 corners in their last six. Carracedo's likely return on the right wing fits Córdoba's wide game, but Ania admits he does not know how Oviedo's new coach will set up away, so nothing firm moves it and I stay at 11.5.

cards.text: The numbers say 7.1 cards, raised for both sides' recent bookings (23 and 21 in their last six) and for referee Daniel Palencia, who averages 5.8 cards a game against a 5.3 league average. Two mid-table sides chasing the play-offs and Ania facing his old club add some edge, but that is the same picture the numbers see, so I stay at 7.1.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.9 shots, already well above a usual game for both teams' recent shooting (95 and 103 in their last six). Raúl González wants a pressing, direct Oviedo that shot a lot from distance against Girona, and Córdoba keep attacking at home; that matches the numbers, so I stay at 31.9.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.6 shots on target, boosted for both sides' accurate recent shooting. Reina's absence is already counted and Enzo Pérez comes straight back into Oviedo's midfield, while Córdoba's front line around Percan is unchanged, so I stay at 10.6.

401882298.overall: Sporting (8th, 23 points, two games without a win and over a month without a home win) host Las Palmas (11th, 20 points), three points behind them. Nicolás Larcamón is badly short: Juan Otero and Àlex Corredera are banned and Alejo Sarco and Manu Rodríguez injured (all in the numbers), and Antonio Casas, César Gelabert, Pablo García and Konrad de la Fuente are also injured, which the numbers do not know; Andrés Ferrari, back from a broken fibula, is set to start up front. Albert Sánchez's Las Palmas travel with seven absences: Opoku (banned) and most of the injured are counted, but Ale García and Cedeño are not; Herzog and Pezzolesi are back from Spain duty and Viti and Sergio Ruiz are still not in the squad. Dámaso Arcediano Monescillo is now confirmed as referee and his record is now in the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.2 goals and already cut Sporting for Otero, Corredera and Sarco. I lean lower to about 2.1 because Sporting are also without Antonio Casas, Gelabert, Pablo García and Konrad, so the attack leans on academy players and Ferrari in his first start since March, and Las Palmas lose Ale García and Cedeño as well.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners, close to both sides' recent levels. Sporting will push for the home win their fans demand, but with wide attackers like Konrad and Pablo García out that does not clearly add corners, and Las Palmas keep the same midfield of Loiodice, Kirian and Fuster, so I stay at 9.4.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.6 cards, raised for both sides' recent bookings (21 each in their last six) and now also for referee Dámaso Arcediano Monescillo, who averages 5.7 cards a game. My earlier small lift was only for the referee, which the numbers now count, so I drop it; the tense home mood is already in the momentum figures and I stay at 5.6.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.8 shots, with a boost for Sporting's 86 shots in their last six. That form came with Casas, Gelabert and Pablo García, who are now injured on top of the counted absences, so I trim it to about 23.8.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.3 shots on target. With most of Sporting's regular forwards out and a returning Ferrari short of rhythm, and Las Palmas missing Ale García too, I lower it to about 7.9.

401883109.overall: Girona (4th) and Eibar (5th) are level on 24 points, so this is a direct fight for the play-off places; Girona won 2-1 at Oviedo last time out, while Eibar have gone five league games without a win despite creating plenty. Match-day checks found no new absences: Quique Álvarez has Vanat and Asprilla back from international duty but is short at the back, with Àlex Moreno banned and Furtado, Bryan Gil and Jastin García injured (all in the numbers), plus Javi Boñar (injured) and Holmes Junior (Spain Under-18), which the numbers don't know, so Abdul Mumin is expected at left-back. Jokin Aranbarri's Eibar miss only Gift, Imanol and Bernat and plan to stay compact and break quickly; Arbilla is one yellow from a ban. Alejandro Morilla of the Navarre committee referees, and his low card record is already in the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.2 goals and already add for Àlex Moreno's absence from Girona's defence and take a little off for Bryan Gil and Jastin García. I still lean slightly higher, to about 2.3, because Girona are also without Boñar and Holmes Junior and are expected to use Mumin, a centre-back, at left-back against an Eibar side Quique Álvarez calls dangerous on the counter; no match-day news changed that.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners, already lifted for Eibar conceding 44 corners in their last six. Aranbarri plans to sit compact and defend his box when Girona have the ball, which fits the home-heavy split the numbers already show (5.9 to 3.5), so I stay at 9.4.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.0 cards and include referee Alejandro Morilla, who averages 4.9 cards a game against a 5.3 average, a cut of about 7%. The play-off stakes and Arbilla playing on four yellows point slightly up, Morilla's calm record slightly down, and both are close to what the numbers see, so I stay at 5.0.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.2 shots, already lifted for both sides' recent shooting (Eibar 91 in their last six). Girona's patched defence could give Eibar a little more, but Eibar will spend long spells defending deep while Girona's front line is close to full strength with Vanat back and Carles Pérez, Abel Ruiz and Pyshchur expected, so I stay at 28.2.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.1 shots on target and already count Eibar's accurate recent shooting (35 on target in six). With Girona missing Boñar and Holmes Junior on top of the counted ban, and a centre-back likely at left-back, Eibar's quick vertical attacks should find a little more, so I nudge it to about 9.4.

401883304.overall: Celta Fortuna (18th, 13 points, one win in ten) host Real Valladolid (14th, 18 points, six off the play-offs) at Balaídos in a match both sides need. Celta's reserve side play fast, open football but leak goals; centre-backs Joel López and Ribes are back from bans, Hugo Cuenca is now reported out after returning from Paraguay duty with discomfort, and Antañón is a doubt after travelling with the first team to the Bernabéu; Gavián, Somuah and Mateo Sobral are out (in the numbers). Valladolid, winners of their last two away games, miss Ojeda (banned) and Latasa (both in the numbers) plus right-back Trilli (not in the numbers), and Fran Escribá again stressed controlling the tempo against a young side. José Antonio Sánchez Villalobos referees and his high card record is already in the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals, already boosting Valladolid for 14 goals in their last six and trimming them for Latasa and Ojeda. I lean slightly lower, to about 2.6, because Escribá wants a controlled game rather than an end-to-end one and Celta get two first-choice centre-backs, Joel López and Ribes, back from bans; Celta's leaky record (26 conceded) keeps the size small.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.3 corners and already add for Valladolid's recent corners (39 in six) against a Celta side that conceded 47. Trilli's absence takes away one of Valladolid's attacking full-backs, but Alejo is a like-for-like replacement, so nothing points either way and I stay at 9.3.

cards.text: The numbers say 7.9 cards and include referee José Antonio Sánchez Villalobos, who averages 6.2 cards a game against a 5.3 average (+21%), on top of Celta's heavy recent booking. A tense game between a side in the drop zone and one chasing the play-offs fits what the numbers already see, so I stay at 7.9.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.7 shots, already lifted for Valladolid's recent shooting (88 in six) and Celta's openness. Escribá's caution points slightly down and Celta's young, fast side slightly up, while Cuenca's absence and Antañón's doubt are too small to move it, so I stay at 27.7.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.8 shots on target, boosted for Valladolid's 39 on target in their last six. Without Latasa (counted) Escribá has to find another option up front, and Celta keep their main scorer Álvaro Marín, so nothing new points either way and I stay at 9.8.

401876395.overall: A relegation six-pointer opens the round: Troyes are 17th with 8 points and Le Havre last with 2 after six straight league defeats. Valérien Ismaël takes charge of Le Havre for the first time; his past sides pressed hard and he is still choosing between a back three and a back four. Le Havre's own preview lists Pembélé, Rassoul Ndiaye, Nakamura and Mosengo out and Ouziad doubtful, with Jelert back, while Mpasi, Mambimbi and Zagadou are long-term absentees. For Troyes, Junior Diaz is suspended (already counted) and forward Yacouba Koné is a doubt; Troyes have scored only 7 league goals, and Ligue 1's own figures show these two have the league's lowest shot conversion. Referee Jérémie Pignard (4.4 cards a game) is already in the numbers; no match-day news changed the view.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.3 goals. Troyes have scored just 7 in 10 league games and may lack forward Koné, and these are the two sides with the lowest shot conversion in Ligue 1, while Ismaël's first job will be to tighten a Le Havre side missing four midfielders. I go a little lower, to about 2.2.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.7 corners, with Troyes at home doing most of the pushing. Neither side's style changes much for this: Troyes build slowly and Le Havre will defend deep under a coach in his first game, which the numbers already reflect, so I stay at 8.7.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.8 cards and already add Pignard's strict record (+17%). On top of that this is a bottom-two scrap where both sides need points badly and Ismaël's teams are known for intensity and pressing, which the numbers' stakes flags do not cover; a small lift to about 5.0.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.8 shots. Troyes create few big chances and Le Havre will be careful, but both will also have to chase points late on, so the two pull against each other and I stay at 24.8.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 7.7 shots on target. Troyes have the league's weakest attack and may be without Koné, and Le Havre's forwards get little support with Ndiaye, Nakamura and Mosengo out, so I trim slightly to about 7.5.

401876398.overall: Leaders PSG (23 points, five straight league wins) visit sixth-placed Nice (17 points), who have won five of their last six league games under Olivier Pantaloni. Dembélé, Marquinhos, Nuno Mendes and Akliouche are back in the PSG squad, but with Roma at the Parc on Wednesday the latest French reports (VIPSG, 433foot, Paris-Supporters) expect a reshuffled XI: Doué fully rested after a muscle alert with France, Hakimi and Pacho rested, and Mayulu, Ndjantou, Ferran Torres and Godts starting, with the returning stars on the bench. The numbers only take Kvaratskhelia off for PSG, so they still assume a near first-choice side. Nice are without Abdelmonem (hamstring) plus long-term absentees Bombito, Abergel and Mendy, all already counted, while Boudaoui and Abdi may return and Wahi leads the line. Referee Jérôme Brisard (4.2 cards a game) is already in the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals, with PSG's strong scoring run and Kvaratskhelia's absence (-4%) already counted. Since yesterday the reports add Hakimi and Pacho to Doué among those rested, so PSG are expected to start without Doué, Hakimi and Kvaratskhelia and with Dembélé on the bench; I deepen my trim from -2 to -4, to about 3.0.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.6 corners, driven by PSG's possession against a Nice back three with wing-backs Clauss and Nkounkou. Rotation changes who attacks rather than how much PSG push Nice back, and Nice's form and missing defenders are already in the numbers, so I stay at 9.6.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.5 cards and already include Jérôme Brisard's slightly above-average record, Nice's recent rise in cards and PSG's low count. A younger PSG side could commit a few more fouls, but nothing points clearly to a heated game, so I stay at 3.5.

shots.text: The numbers say 29.7 shots, already raised for both sides' recent shooting. PSG will still have most of the ball, but a starting XI without Doué, Hakimi and Dembélé, the players who drive much of their shooting, should create a little less in the first hour; I cut to about 28.8.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 12.3 shots on target and already give PSG +20% for 60 on target in their last six, a run built by the first-choice attack. With Doué rested and Dembélé expected on the bench, I trim to about 11.8.

401876399.overall: Monaco (7th, 16 points) have gone five league games without a win under Filipe Luís and have not kept a clean sheet in eight, while Auxerre (15th, 10 points) under Will Still have lost their last two, including 5-1 at Strasbourg, and have the league's worst defence with 24 conceded. Golovin (calf, two to three weeks per Nice-Matin via Maxifoot), Idumbo and Ansu Fati are out and counted; centre-back Mawissa is still a doubt with a groin problem (beIN, Tufutbolero), and Coulibaly is available because his ban starts next round. Auxerre's striker Danny Namaso is listed out (beIN, Camfoot), as the numbers already assumed, alongside Okoh, Dioussé, Fofana and Zaddy; beIN also lists centre-back Akpa among the absentees, though Sports Mole still has him in its lineup, and Dioubaté is back from suspension. Auxerre have not beaten Monaco in 12 meetings and are expected to sit compact and break through Archer (six league goals). Referee Jérémy Stinat (4.1 cards a game) is already in the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals and already take almost a fifth off Auxerre's attack for Namaso and some off Monaco for Golovin and Idumbo. New since this morning, one report (beIN) lists Auxerre centre-back Akpa as absent and Monaco's Mawissa is still only a doubt, neither of which the numbers know; with two leaky defences that is a small nudge up, to about 2.86.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.8 corners, with Monaco expected to have most of the ball against Auxerre's back three and wing-backs. Filipe Luís wants more risk going forward, but that is how Monaco usually play at home against a side that sits deep, so I stay at 9.8.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.5 cards and already add Stinat's slightly strict record (4.1 a game) and past meetings. Dioubaté returns for Auxerre and Coulibaly plays before his ban, but nothing points to a heated game, so I stay at 4.5.

shots.text: The numbers say 23.9 shots. Filipe Luís admits his attack has struggled without Golovin, which is already counted, and Auxerre will sit compact and counter through Archer; nothing new points either way, so I stay at 23.9.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.3 shots on target. With Namaso out as the numbers assumed, Archer is Auxerre's main threat, and Monaco's poor finishing in five winless games is already in their recent record, so I stay at 9.3.

401876403.overall: Lens (11th) and Toulouse (12th) are level on 13 points, but Lens have lost three in a row, including 9-1 at home to Como in the Champions League, and Didier Digard takes charge for the first time after Yannick Cahuzac's sacking. Lensois.com's match-day preview confirms forward Franjo Ivanović (hurt late in the week) and defender Jonathan Gradit are out, neither counted by the numbers, on top of Édouard, Bulatović and Nawrocki, who are; Sima and Ganiou are back in the squad but expected on the bench (Eurofootnews still calls Sima uncertain). Lens are expected in a 3-4-3 with Thauvin, Hazard and Sotoca up front. Toulouse (Jens Berthel Askou) miss Messali (counted) and possibly Abu Francis, with Dønnum back and Tengstedt leading the line in a 4-4-2. Referee Bastien Dechepy (4.4 cards a game) is already in the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.9 goals, partly because Lens have leaked heavily lately. Ivanović is confirmed out, which the numbers don't know, leaving Thauvin, Hazard and Sotoca with Sima only fit for the bench, and a new coach after a 9-1 defeat will want a solid first game; Gradit's absence at the back pulls slightly the other way, so I keep a small trim to about 2.8.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners. Lens are expected in a 3-4-3 with wing-backs Aguilar and Udol and Digard wants play down the flanks, while Toulouse play a 4-4-2; that is close to how both usually play, so I stay at 9.4.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.8 cards and already add Dechepy's strict record (about +15%) and past meetings. A first game under a new coach brings energy but also more attention to discipline, and nothing points either way, so I stay at 4.8.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.9 shots. Digard's pressing could add a few for Lens, but Toulouse create a lot without finishing and Lens are short of fit forwards; these balance out, so I stay at 24.9.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.8 shots on target. With Ivanović out, Sima only on the bench and Édouard injured (counted), Lens have less sharpness up front than the numbers allow for, so I trim a little, to about 8.5.

401876402.overall: Second-placed Lille (21 points), with the league's best defence and unbeaten in five, host fifth-placed Lyon (17 points), who have lost three away league games in a row. Lyon start under new coach Carlos Vicens with a 21-man squad including Tagliafico, Kango and Tolisso; Clinton Mata (muscle) is out, which the numbers don't count, while Openda, Sulc, Morton and Ouédraogo are out and counted. For Lille, Tiago Santos and Igamane are out and counted; reports differ on Ayase Ueda (fit per Olympique-et-Lyonnais, still doubtful per Sports Mole), but the numbers never counted him as missing and Haraldsson is expected to lead the line either way. Lille host Bayern in the Champions League next week, Lyon's away fans are banned, and François Letexier (4.0 cards a game) referees, already counted.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.2 goals, with the missing forwards on both sides already taken off. Ueda's status changes nothing because the numbers never counted him out; the small nudge comes from Lyon losing right-back Mata, a regular the numbers don't know is missing, to about 2.24.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.7 corners. Both sides play a 4-3-3 with wide forwards, and Vicens has kept Lyon's back four, so I see no reason to move from 9.7.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.3 cards, with Letexier's near-average record already in. Lyon's travelling fans are banned and nothing points to a heated game under a new Lyon coach, so I stay at 4.3.

shots.text: The numbers say 21.9 shots. Lille's possession game and Vicens wanting a higher press could add a few, but Lyon are without Openda and Sulc up front (counted), so I stay at 21.9.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.3 shots on target. Haraldsson is expected to start up front for Lille whether or not Ueda is fit, which is how the numbers see Lille's attack, and Lyon are without Openda and Sulc (counted), so I stay at 8.3.

401876396.overall: Strasbourg (14th, 10 points, five defeats in six) sacked Hugo Oliveira this week and Vítor Matos takes charge for the first time at the Meinau, promising pressing, attacking football. Match-day previews (Get French Football News citing L'Équipe, Kickfootball) confirm Giovanni Reyna, full-back Oso, Baldé and striker Panichelli are out; only Panichelli and Baldé are counted by the numbers, and goalkeeper Jørgensen is expected to start after his international-duty knock. Brest (9th, 15 points) arrive after beating Lorient and Lyon without conceding, missing only Chardonnet and Le Guen (counted), with Ajorque leading the line against his old club and Brest unbeaten in their last four visits to Strasbourg. Azzedine Souifi referees; the numbers know only four of his top-flight games and blend them with an average record.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.3 goals, a high figure driven by Strasbourg's open games. Matos wants to attack, but Reyna and Oso are confirmed out on top of Panichelli and Baldé (only those two are counted), so Strasbourg's attack is thinner than the numbers think; I trim slightly to about 3.2.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.8 corners. Both teams are expected in a 4-2-3-1 or 4-3-3, and a pressing start under Matos is close to how Strasbourg already play, so I stay at 8.8.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.5 cards. Souifi has only four games in the numbers, which already blend his record with an average referee, and Matos' pressing could bring a few fouls but nothing points to a heated game, so I stay at 3.5.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.9 shots. A new coach demanding intensity at home could add a few, while Reyna's and Oso's absences take some away, so I stay at 24.9.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.8 shots on target. Without Reyna, Oso and Panichelli, Strasbourg lose much of their finishing and creativity, more than the numbers count, with Harder expected up front alone, so I trim slightly to about 8.6.

401876397.overall: Third-placed Paris FC (20 points, three behind PSG and one behind Lille) host Angers (17th, 8 points), who are winless in five and have not scored in their last three league games. Liam Rosenior has a near-complete squad: Ikoné and Sangui are out (both counted), centre-back Chergui (knee) and Adama Camara (hamstring) are doubts, and Lassine Sinayoko, who scored the winner at Auxerre, leads the line. Angers' Stéphane Gilli, Paris FC's coach until February, misses the suspended Lefort (counted) and Bané Diatta (counted) plus Oumar Pona, ill after Mali U23 duty; Sports Mole and Soccernet say striker El Ouazzani is back, while The Stats Zone still calls him a doubt. Angers are expected to sit deep, and referee Aurélien Petit (2.5 cards a game in four top-flight games) is already in the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals and already add a little to Paris FC's side for Lefort's absence in the Angers defence. Angers have scored only three in five and none in three, but El Ouazzani looks available again and Paris FC have conceded in their recent home games, while Sinayoko is in form; these pull in opposite directions, so I stay at 2.6.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.8 corners, already trimmed because Angers have won few corners lately. Against a deep, struggling Angers side Paris FC should have long spells of pressure out wide through Kebbal, Matondo and Simon, which tends to produce corners, so I nudge it up to about 9.1.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.2 cards and already take some off for Aurélien Petit, who has shown only 2.5 cards a game so far. Gilli facing the club that sacked him in February adds a little edge, but it is not a rivalry and nothing points to a heated game, so I stay at 3.2.
